data.label: User browser
data.description: Existing client reference for a signed-in user. Not provisioned.

data.label: RAG web app
data.description: Hosts the browser app from private S3 assets behind CloudFront access control. Signs users in with authorization code + PKCE, then calls the API with an access token and shows answers with citations.

data.label: User pool
data.description: Admin-created users with required software-token MFA. Issues scoped access tokens. Identity-to-employee-region mappings live in the catalog. Users are onboarded through the generated operator tool; no passwords are stored in the diagram.

data.label: RAG API
data.description: Bounded authenticated HTTP API with a JWT browser route. Unknown identities fail closed. No anonymous access.

data.label: Keyword retrieval and answer
data.description: Runs keyword search over the catalog, filters by the caller's ACL and region, rechecks document revisions, calls the model and returns a cited answer, or abstains when nothing grounds it. Owns its execution role, logs, version and alias.

data.label: Document catalog and ACLs
data.description: Up to 100 small synthetic UTF-8 documents with explicit per-document ACLs and identity mappings. Ingestion: an operator loads documents through the generated conditional management tool. Caller roles cannot write to it.

data.label: Foundation model
data.description: A direct foundation model reached through Converse. The model ID, model access, quotas and regional availability are still unselected and unverified. Locally, model replies are mocked.

brief.application: Use AWS for this synthetic architecture qualification. Answer questions over a small synthetic document collection with citations. Include ingestion, retrieval, model runtime, identity enforcement and an authenticated application. Use bounded keyword retrieval for this first test and keep all source permissions. Draw the complete end-to-end architecture with concrete service choices and connected flows. Explain the first local test, distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation, and ask one useful missing-decision question. Do not reduce this application to storage to satisfy generator coverage. Do not invent successful deployment or approved region/account access.

decisions.subject: design.bounded-keyword-rag-on-aws-with-an-authenticated-web-app
decisions.title: Bounded keyword RAG on AWS with an authenticated web app
decisions.context: Scope: a citation-backed question-answering app over a synthetic collection of up to 100 small UTF-8 documents. Flow: browser (existing client) → CloudFront web app → Cognito (PKCE, MFA) → API Gateway JWT route → Lambda keyword retrieval → DynamoDB catalog with explicit ACLs → Bedrock Converse. Ingestion uses the catalog's generated operator management tool. Assumptions: region, country and Bedrock model ID are not decided yet; model access and quotas are unverified; this is keyword retrieval, not vector search. Nothing has been deployed.
decisions.decision: Drawn while talking as design revision 2.

needs.statement: Proposed: answers may only use documents the signed-in user is allowed to read. If the user's identity is unknown, the request is refused.
needs.rationale: If permissions leak, people can see content they shouldn't. This is the main thing the qualification needs to prove.
needs.basis: User: "keep all source permissions" and "identity enforcement".

needs.statement: Proposed: every answer cites the documents it came from. If no permitted document supports an answer, the app abstains.
needs.rationale: Without citations, nobody can check an answer, and unsupported answers erode trust.
needs.basis: User: "Answer questions over a small synthetic document collection with citations".

needs.statement: Proposed: keep mocked local model results separate from real Bedrock validation. Real validation needs an approved model ID, model access and quotas in the chosen region.
needs.rationale: A mock can't show answer quality or prove that the model is available.
needs.basis: User: "distinguish mocked model behavior from actual model validation".
